HOW IT WILL WORK

Clear steps.
No guessing.

We’re shaping a straightforward service with our specialist testing partner. The final collection, reporting and support arrangements will be clear before ordering opens.

01 · CHOOSE

Understand your options.

Compare the panel, collection method, price and limitations. Ask a healthcare professional if you need advice on which tests are appropriate.

02 · COLLECT

The right sample, properly.

We’re trialling finger-prick kits and an upper-arm device for home collection. Supported tests and the device’s small extra charge are being confirmed. Complete currently needs a professional venous sample.

03 · UNDERSTAND

See the result and next step.

The intended journey brings secure results access and clear next-step guidance together. Reporting and clinical follow-up responsibilities must be confirmed before launch.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

The useful questions.

How do I choose between the three?

Start with the areas each panel covers and the way the sample is taken. More markers do not automatically mean a more appropriate test. These pages explain the proposed options; they do not provide a personalised clinical recommendation.

What are the two home collection options?

We’re trialling a finger-prick kit and a device placed on your upper arm. The aim is to offer another way to collect your sample at home. A small extra charge is planned for the upper-arm device; the amount and availability are being confirmed.

Can I use either collection option for every test?

Supported tests are still being checked with our specialist testing partner. The upper-arm option is in trial. Availability and supported tests will be confirmed before ordering opens. Complete currently requires a professional venous sample at a clinic or nurse home visit.

Will this tell me everything is fine?

No. A blood test is a snapshot of the markers tested, not a complete assessment of your health. A result inside a reference range does not explain every symptom or rule out every condition.

Do I need a test because I use a GLP-1 medicine?

These panels are being considered as part of a wider support offer. They are not presented as mandatory for everyone using GLP-1 medicines and do not replace your prescriber’s assessment or monitoring advice.

What happens if my sample cannot be analysed?

The final service information will explain repeat-kit arrangements, support, any charges and refunds before ordering opens. Repeat-kit costs and response times will be explained before ordering opens.

Can I order a test now?

Ordering is not open yet. Prices, final panel profiles, collection availability and the agreed reporting and follow-up arrangements still need to be completed before launch.

YOUR HEALTH, KEPT TOGETHER

It belongs in My Timber.

Testing should connect with the reason you started. Explore the proposed place for test progress and secure results access alongside your everyday SHIFT journey.

SHIFT BLOODS · THE CORE PICTURE

Baseline Health

Start with the essentials. A focused look at cholesterol, liver function and kidney function essentials.

BaselineAdvancedComplete
THE PURPOSE

Know what you’re choosing.

A straightforward starting point if you want to understand these core areas without choosing a wider panel.

HOW IT FITS YOUR SHIFT

Your SHIFT is about more than a number on the scales. These core checks connect with heart health, weight, waist and blood pressure, alongside the food and movement habits you are working on.

This proposed panel does not include HbA1c, thyroid or testosterone testing.

PROPOSED PANEL CONTENT

What’s in the picture.

Open an area to see the proposed markers. The final configured profile will be checked before ordering opens. Some markers appear in more than one group; we have not added them together to inflate a total.

CholesterolBlood fats linked to heart health, alongside your food, movement and weight goals.

The balance of fats in your blood helps inform a heart-health assessment. High cholesterol often has no symptoms, so how you feel is not a reliable guide to your level.

In your SHIFT: The scales are only part of the story. Put cholesterol alongside your waist, blood pressure, food and activity when discussing longer-term health.

NHS: cholesterol testing ↗

The proposed markers

  • Total cholesterol
  • HDL cholesterol
  • HDL as a percentage of total
  • LDL cholesterol
  • Non-HDL cholesterol
  • Triglycerides
Liver functionLiver-health markers that matter when considering weight, alcohol and metabolic health.

These markers can help flag liver problems. Fatty liver can be linked to excess weight and metabolic health, while alcohol and other causes also need consideration. Blood results alone do not provide the whole diagnosis.

In your SHIFT: If weight, waist size or drinking is part of your SHIFT, liver health belongs in that conversation too. Results need interpretation rather than an assumption that every change is down to your weight.

NHS: fatty liver and metabolic health ↗

The proposed markers

  • Alanine aminotransferase (ALT)
  • Albumin
  • Alkaline phosphatase (ALP)
  • Bilirubin
  • Gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)
  • Globulins
  • Total protein
Kidney function essentialsHelps assess filtering, alongside the wider picture of blood pressure and diabetes risk.

Creatinine is used to estimate how well your kidneys filter waste, reported as eGFR. This is part of a kidney assessment; repeat blood tests or urine testing may also be needed.

In your SHIFT: Kidney health connects with blood pressure and diabetes. These markers can add useful context to a wider health review; they are not a standalone hydration score or proof that all is well.

NHS: assessing kidney function ↗

The proposed markers

  • Creatinine
  • Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)
  • Urea
TAKING THE SAMPLE

A sample taken at home.

Finger-prick at home

Collect your sample using the finger-prick kit and return it for laboratory analysis.

Standard home collection option. Total price being finalised.

Upper-arm collection device — trial

Prefer to avoid a finger-prick kit? This device collects the sample from your upper arm, at home. We’re trialling the option and confirming supported tests and availability.

Small additional charge planned. Amount being finalised.

Put off by finger-prick kits? Meet the upper-arm option →

Follow the instructions supplied for your exact test. Preparation and collection timing depend on the panel and will be confirmed before you order.

THE HONEST LIMITS

A result needs context.

These tests measure the markers listed, not every aspect of your health. Your symptoms, history, medicines and the circumstances of the sample matter.

Persistent or worrying symptoms deserve a conversation with your GP. Do not wait for a private test if you need medical care.

RESULTS & SUPPORT

Understand what happens afterwards.

We’re building the testing journey with our specialist testing partner. Before ordering opens, you will be told who provides the test, how to access the report, what review is included and who handles important findings.

The final service information will also set out collection support, insufficient samples, repeat kits, turnaround expectations, cancellation and refunds.

SHIFT BLOODS · A WIDER VIEW

Advanced Health

Look a little further. The core areas, with thyroid, selected vitamins and minerals, and testosterone.

BaselineAdvancedComplete
THE PURPOSE

Know what you’re choosing.

A wider proposed panel for someone who wants to explore these additional areas alongside the core biochemistry.

HOW IT FITS YOUR SHIFT

Feeling better matters as much as weighing less. The added checks create space for a proper conversation about energy, food intake and hormonal concerns, without assuming every symptom has the same cause.

Testosterone results need clinical context. This proposed panel does not include HbA1c or a full blood count.

What’s in the picture.

CholesterolBlood fats linked to heart health, alongside your food, movement and weight goals.

The balance of fats in your blood helps inform a heart-health assessment. High cholesterol often has no symptoms, so how you feel is not a reliable guide to your level.

In your SHIFT: The scales are only part of the story. Put cholesterol alongside your waist, blood pressure, food and activity when discussing longer-term health.

  • Total cholesterol
  • HDL cholesterol
  • HDL as a percentage of total
  • LDL cholesterol
  • Non-HDL cholesterol
  • Triglycerides

  • Bilirubin

  • Globulins
  • Total protein
Kidney function essentialsHelps assess filtering, alongside the wider picture of blood pressure and diabetes risk.

Creatinine is used to estimate how well your kidneys filter waste, reported as eGFR. This is part of a kidney assessment; repeat blood tests or urine testing may also be needed.

In your SHIFT: Kidney health connects with blood pressure and diabetes. These markers can add useful context to a wider health review; they are not a standalone hydration score or proof that all is well.

NHS: assessing kidney function ↗

The proposed markers

  • Creatinine
  • Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)
  • Urea
Thyroid functionHormone checks that can help investigate tiredness or weight changes, with clinical context.

Thyroid hormones help regulate how your body uses energy. An underactive thyroid can cause tiredness and weight gain, but these symptoms have many possible explanations.

In your SHIFT: Persistent low energy or unexplained weight changes deserve more than a guess about motivation. These checks can support a clinical investigation without assuming the thyroid is the cause.

NHS: thyroid symptoms and testing ↗

The proposed markers

  • Free thyroxine (T4)
  • Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
  • Triiodothyronine (T3)
Vitamins & mineralsSelected nutrients that add context to blood health, tiredness and the food you are managing to eat.

For example, vitamin B12 and folate are important for healthy blood cells, and deficiencies can contribute to tiredness. The listed markers check selected areas; they do not measure the overall quality of your diet.

In your SHIFT: Eating less should still mean eating well. If your appetite or food choices have changed, this is useful context for a nutrition conversation. Results do not automatically mean you need supplements.

NHS: B12, folate and blood health ↗

The proposed markers

  • Adjusted calcium
  • Albumin
  • Calcium
  • Ferritin
  • Active vitamin B12
  • Folate (vitamin B9)
TestosteroneHormonal context for energy or sex-drive concerns. One result does not mean you need TRT.

Testosterone testing can be part of investigating persistent symptoms such as reduced sex drive or low energy. Symptoms, collection timing and any need for repeat testing must be considered together.

In your SHIFT: This connects with the SHIFT Health approach to energy and testosterone: investigate properly, including sleep, stress and wider health, rather than jumping straight to treatment.

NHS: symptoms, testosterone and assessment ↗

The proposed markers

  • Testosterone

SHIFT BLOODS · THE BROADER PANEL

Complete Health

Build a broader picture. A broader proposed panel, including HbA1c, a full blood count and additional nutritional and hormonal markers.

BaselineAdvancedComplete
THE PURPOSE

Know what you’re choosing.

The widest of these proposed options. It needs a venous blood sample taken by a professional, rather than a home finger-prick kit.

HOW IT FITS YOUR SHIFT

A broader panel can support a wider clinical conversation about blood sugar, blood health, nutrition and hormones. It is not automatically the better choice: the tests should fit the question you are trying to answer.

Complete is the name of this panel. It cannot check for every condition or replace a clinical assessment.

PROPOSED PANEL CONTENT

What’s in the picture.

Open an area to see the proposed markers. The final configured profile will be checked before ordering opens. Some markers appear in more than one group; we have not added them together to inflate a total.

CholesterolBlood fats linked to heart health, alongside your food, movement and weight goals.

In your SHIFT: The scales are only part of the story. Put cholesterol alongside your waist, blood pressure, food and activity when discussing longer-term health.

NHS: cholesterol testing ↗

The proposed markers

  • Total cholesterol
  • HDL cholesterol
  • HDL as a percentage of total
  • LDL cholesterol
  • Non-HDL cholesterol
  • Triglycerides
Liver functionLiver-health markers that matter when considering weight, alcohol and metabolic health.

These markers can help flag liver problems. Fatty liver can be linked to excess weight and metabolic health, while alcohol and other causes also need consideration. Blood results alone do not provide the whole diagnosis.

In your SHIFT: If weight, waist size or drinking is part of your SHIFT, liver health belongs in that conversation too. Results need interpretation rather than an assumption that every change is down to your weight.

NHS: fatty liver and metabolic health ↗

The proposed markers

  • Alanine aminotransferase (ALT)
  • Albumin
  • Alkaline phosphatase (ALP)
  • Bilirubin
  • Gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)
  • Globulins
  • Total protein
Kidney function essentialsHelps assess filtering, alongside the wider picture of blood pressure and diabetes risk.

Creatinine is used to estimate how well your kidneys filter waste, reported as eGFR. This is part of a kidney assessment; repeat blood tests or urine testing may also be needed.

In your SHIFT: Kidney health connects with blood pressure and diabetes. These markers can add useful context to a wider health review; they are not a standalone hydration score or proof that all is well.

NHS: assessing kidney function ↗

The proposed markers

  • Creatinine
  • Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)
  • Urea
HbA1cA view of average blood sugar over roughly two to three months, rather than a single moment.

HbA1c can help assess longer-term blood sugar and is used in diabetes diagnosis and monitoring. A healthcare professional needs to interpret it in context, and it is not suitable for every situation.

In your SHIFT: This connects directly with the metabolic side of the journey: looking beyond body weight to blood sugar, food, activity and the care you may need.

NHS: blood sugar and HbA1c ↗

The proposed markers

  • HbA1c
Vitamins & mineralsSelected nutrients that add context to blood health, tiredness and the food you are managing to eat.

For example, vitamin B12 and folate are important for healthy blood cells, and deficiencies can contribute to tiredness. The listed markers check selected areas; they do not measure the overall quality of your diet.

In your SHIFT: Eating less should still mean eating well. If your appetite or food choices have changed, this is useful context for a nutrition conversation. Results do not automatically mean you need supplements.

NHS: B12, folate and blood health ↗

The proposed markers

  • Adjusted calcium
  • Albumin
  • Calcium
  • Ferritin
  • Active vitamin B12
  • Folate (vitamin B9)
  • Magnesium
  • Vitamin D
Cardiovascular risk markerHigh-sensitivity CRP measures an inflammation marker; it does not explain the cause on its own.

CRP is a non-specific marker of inflammation. The high-sensitivity measurement needs interpretation alongside your health history and other findings, rather than being treated as a diagnosis.

In your SHIFT: It is another piece of a wider clinical conversation, not a score for how healthy you are or proof that a food, exercise plan or medicine is working.

NHS laboratory: CRP and its limitations ↗

The proposed markers

  • High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP)
Iron statusLooks at iron stores and availability, which can be relevant when investigating tiredness or anaemia.

The proposed iron profile includes several markers rather than relying on a single number. Abnormal results need interpretation and, where appropriate, investigation of the cause.

In your SHIFT: If low energy is getting in the way of everyday life or activity, a proper assessment matters. Do not assume tiredness is simply lack of fitness or start iron supplements on that basis.

NHS: blood tests and anaemia ↗

The proposed markers

  • Ferritin
  • Serum iron
  • Total iron-binding capacity (TIBC)
  • Transferrin saturation
  • Unsaturated iron-binding capacity (UIBC)
Free testosterone & SHBGAdds context to testosterone availability, rather than turning one hormone number into a diagnosis.

SHBG is a protein that binds sex hormones. Free testosterone and related calculations can contribute to a fuller hormonal assessment when interpreted appropriately.

In your SHIFT: The aim is a better clinical conversation about persistent symptoms. These results do not automatically establish a deficiency or a need for TRT.

NHS laboratory: SHBG and testosterone ↗

The proposed markers

  • Free androgen index (FAI)
  • Free testosterone
  • Sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG)
Thyroid functionHormone checks that can help investigate tiredness or weight changes, with clinical context.

Thyroid hormones help regulate how your body uses energy. An underactive thyroid can cause tiredness and weight gain, but these symptoms have many possible explanations.

In your SHIFT: Persistent low energy or unexplained weight changes deserve more than a guess about motivation. These checks can support a clinical investigation without assuming the thyroid is the cause.

NHS: thyroid symptoms and testing ↗

The proposed markers

  • Free thyroxine (T4)
  • Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
  • Triiodothyronine (T3)
CortisolA hormone measurement affected by sample timing and clinical circumstances, not a day-to-day stress score.

Cortisol follows a daily rhythm, and the collection time matters when interpreting a result. A single measurement cannot explain how stressed you feel or diagnose the cause of fatigue.

In your SHIFT: Sleep, routine and stress still deserve attention in their own right. This result needs a specific clinical question and the right interpretation, rather than a promise to explain everything.

NHS laboratory: cortisol and sample timing ↗

The proposed markers

  • Cortisol
Full blood countLooks at blood cells, including checks that can help investigate anaemia and tiredness.

A full blood count measures blood-cell numbers and characteristics. It can help investigate conditions such as anaemia, but it does not give an overall immunity rating.

In your SHIFT: When low energy is affecting daily life or making activity harder, the cause matters. Blood-count findings sit alongside your symptoms and history, not a judgement about effort.

NHS: full blood count and other blood tests ↗

The proposed markers

  • Basophils
  • Eosinophils
  • Haematocrit
  • Haemoglobin
  • Lymphocytes
  • Mean corpuscular haemoglobin (MCH)
  • Mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC)
  • Mean corpuscular volume (MCV)
  • Mean platelet volume (MPV)
  • Monocytes
  • Neutrophils
  • Platelets
  • Red cell count
  • Red cell distribution width
  • White cell count

About SHIFT Bloods.

The planned SHIFT Bloods service. Testing and ordering are not open.

What can I explore?

You can explore the proposed Baseline, Advanced and Complete panels, collection differences and an example of the member journey. Choosing a test or changing an example stage does not place an order.

The proposed testing partner

The proposed service is being developed with Vitall Sync, offered by Healthy Human Labs Ltd. The partnership, configured panels, seller/payment model and clinical responsibilities must be confirmed before the service launches. SHIFT does not operate the laboratory or provide clinical interpretation.

Personal information on these pages

These pages have no questionnaire, payment form, live order registration or blood-results import. It stores only your selected test and collection option in your browser’s session storage so you can move between pages and return to your choice. The collection controls do not send these choices to a testing partner or create a test order.

The website’s existing privacy and cookie information also applies. The Bloods selection controls add no marketing trackers.

Before a real service opens

The final service must explain the organisations involved, purposes and legal basis for using information, what is shared, reporting and clinical-review arrangements, retention, individual rights and the support routes. This information does not replace the final test-specific terms or privacy information.

Final panel profiles, retail prices, kit/collection costs, reporting inclusions, significant-result escalation, repeat samples, cancellation and refund arrangements remain launch decisions.

Existing SHIFT policies

The current website has its own privacy information ↗ and terms ↗. Those documents are linked for context; the test-specific service and data-sharing information will be confirmed before ordering opens.
